title: Resolve rolling aggregation leak causing per-model usage divergence
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Symptom: Over the last 48 hours Console per-model breakdown charts have diverged from raw billing counters for a subset of tenants. Symptoms include: (1) spikes in model-specific token counts that do not appear in ingestion raw logs, (2) per-tenant total tokens matching billing but per-model distribution shifted (sum of per-model != per-tenant totals within sliding windows), and (3) alerts from the reconciliation job showing negative deltas during 1-minute windows for some tenant shards. Impact: customers see incorrect per-model cost attribution in Console dashboards and can be billed incorrectly if left unaddressed. Scope: affects tenants with high burst traffic that hit the new aggregator shard-join optimization deployed 2026-03-08 (PR #8124). Not all tenants are affected; pattern correlates with: multi-region routing, late-arriving events, and when requests are subject to token bucket throttling and retry paths. Initial hypothesis: an interaction between the new shard-join optimization (which coalesces short-lived per-shard windows for efficiency) and the rolling-window aggregator's deduplication/watermark logic resulted in some events being double-counted across adjacent windows when late-arriving usage events were replayed across shards. Technical notes: the rolling aggregator groups events by tenant+model and assigns them to minute-aligned windows using ingestion_epoch rounded to minute. The shard-join optimization changed ingest ordering by introducing transient virtual shards and a join layer that re-emitted events with a synthetic shard_id when replaying late events; the aggregator deduped on event_id but the replay path re-assigned event_id for replayed events, causing dedup to fail and leading to double-counting into the next window. Additionally, the rate-limiter path appends a retry_hint header for throttled requests; this header was unintentionally included in the dedup-key building logic in the joiner, causing keys to be inconsistent across initial and replayed events. Repro steps: 1) simulate high-burst tenant with synthetic delayed ingestion (~45s delay) and throttling path; 2) enable shard-join optimization in staging; 3) observe per-model minute buckets showing +-100% discrepancies compared to raw monotonic counters. Logs/artifacts: - Staging trace: tracing.redwood.internal/trace/5421 (replay path) - Grafana panels: grafana.redwood/internal/dashboards/usage-tenant-501 - PR that introduced shard-join: github.com/redwood-inference/ingest@PR8124 - Reconciliation job run: infra-job-usage-recon/2026-03-13-03:20 (shows negative deltas)
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 — Ayesha Patel: Triage: customer impact reported by CS for tenant acme-int. Repro in staging reproduced similar divergence. Marking P0 and assigning to Marco for immediate investigation.

2026-03-10 13:45 — Marco Liu: Root cause analysis in progress. Observed that replayed events have different event_id in joiner path. Found joiner code that appends retry_hint to dedup-key by mistake (line 153 of joiner service). Will try a quick patch to normalize dedup-key generation.

2026-03-11 02:05 — SRE (Janelle Morris): Reconciliation alerts fired repeatedly during overnight window. Temporarily disabled shard-join optimization in staging to prevent further divergence while we develop fix. Not disabling in prod yet — impact limited to specific tenants but risk of billing issues persists.

2026-03-11 16:30 — Marco Liu: Patch created (github PR #8187). Changes: (a) remove retry_hint from dedup-key; (b) ensure dedup-key uses canonical original_event_id when present; (c) add watermark tag to replay events so aggregator can detect late-arrivals. Added unit tests for dedup-key canonicalization.

2026-03-12 09:10 — Product (Elliot Ramos): PM sign-off on rollback plan vs forward-fix. Prefer forward fix with migration if we can guarantee correctness and not cause prolonged backfills. We may need a short maintenance window for historical correction.

2026-03-12 15:40 — Marco Liu: Integration tests green in staging. Running a staged backfill job (backfill-run-2026-03-12-15) to correct 6 hours of drift for affected tenants. Monitoring dashboard shows per-model sums aligning with tenant totals after backfill in staging.

2026-03-13 08:52 — Ayesha Patel: Cross-team sync outcome: SRE to add guardrail alert (recon-alert-high-negative-delta) and telemetry to detect dedup-key scheme mismatches; Data infra to prepare a safe historical repair tool; Product approved forward-fix + migration plan. Release window scheduled 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC low-traffic maintenance.

2026-03-13 22:05 — Marco Liu: Deploy blocked briefly by infrastructure capacity limits for backfill job. Resolved by throttling backfill parallelism and rescheduling. Backfill ETA now 6 hours for prod window. Update: PR #8187 merged to main and queued for release.

2026-03-14 01:45 — SRE (Janelle Morris): Prod deploy started 02:00 UTC. Observability: added temporary dashboards to track (a) dedup-key diversity per-tenant, (b) minute-bucket discrepancies, (c) reconciliation job negative-delta counts.

2026-03-14 09:55 — Marco Liu: Post-deploy check: immediate window shows correction for 87% of previously affected tenants. We continue historical repair. Leaving ticket In Progress until full verification and customer notification complete.

2026-03-14 12:03 — Customer Success (Rohan Patel): Drafted customer notification for tenants where invoices may have slight per-model attribution variance; will provide corrected reports after backfill completes.
resolution_plan: 1) Deploy dedup-key canonicalization and watermark tag (PR #8187). 2) Run constrained historical repair (backfill) for 12h window of highest divergence per tenant using idempotent repair tool that dedups on original_event_id and ingestion_epoch. 3) Add an automated reconciliation alert that fires on >0.5% minute-level negative deltas for any tenant shard for 5 consecutive minutes. 4) Add unit/integration tests that simulate throttling+replay path to prevent regressions. 5) Postmortem and customer outreach with corrected per-model reports and optional credits for affected customers.
acceptance_criteria: All affected tenants show per-model sums equal to tenant totals within 0.1% for the repaired window.
Reconciliation job no longer reports negative deltas for >60 minutes post-fix on any shard.
New tests added and green in CI for replay+dedeup scenarios.
Monitoring alert created and tested; paging threshold validated with SRE.
Customer Success has sent correction notices and attachments for affected invoices.
postmortem_notes: Immediate cause: dedup-key divergence introduced by shard-join replay path and inclusion of retry_hint in key building. Contributing factors: lack of integration tests covering replay+dederivation paths; no guardrail metric for dedup-key cardinality. Long-term mitigations: canonical event_id propagation, stronger contracts between joiner and aggregator, integration test harness for late-arrival scenarios, and a reconciliation SLA that triggers automatic repair if per-model attribution drifts more than threshold. Consider making dedup-key scheme explicit in protocol docs and adding schema versioning to event envelopes.
